paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders,
I'm so sorry to be so late with the Wednesday update. I've been busy, but that's just no excuse. I need to plan better. I repent. I'll do better tomorrow.

We had a super productive day yesterday on Tuesday, and I think we're pretty well positioned now with our food and water supplies. Now, we may never need to use the food storage, but please keep it just in case.

Also be sure to keep getting out to the store every few days to supply yourself with food. If you have challenges, please talk to your district leader. He is called to serve you and has the right to inspiration that can bless you if you will counsel with him.

That is also true about the sister training leaders, the zone leaders, and the assistants to the president. They may not be much older than you. They may even be younger than you, but that doesn't matter.

If you honor and sustain your leaders, the Lord will honor and sustain you. Even when I was a stake president, if I had a problem, I would go to my own bishop for counsel because I knew the Lord is a God of order, and He works through His channels to bring to pass His work and glory.
So please honor, respect, and counsel with your missionary leaders.
Now, when Sister Hughes and I first got to the mission, we met many great missionaries. One missionary, however, really stood out because he was such a hard worker, and he had so much success.
One day I asked him what the secret of his motivation was and how he kept himself so productive in the Lord's work. He said, "It's all about HOP, President."

I said, "HOP? What's HOP?" And he said, "H-O-P. HOP." He said it's an acronym that his grandfather taught him just before he left on his mission. HOP caused this elder to stay focused and faithful right to the very last day of his mission.
So what is HOP?

Well, this faithful missionary explained it this way, and I quote: "If a missionary is HOP, they will be extremely successful no matter what, no matter where they serve, no matter what the situation is."

"H" is for hardworking. If you're hardworking, you're out on time. You don't come back until 9:00 p.m. You talk to everyone no matter the time, place, or situation. You don't stop trying, even if all your appointments fall through. You simply do your very best to be diligent at everything.

There's a quote in Preach My Gospel made by President Ezra Taft Benson, which says: "I've often said one of the greatest secrets of missionary work is work. If a missionary works, he will get the Spirit. If he gets the Spirit, he will teach by the Spirit. If he teaches by the Spirit, he will touch the hearts of the people, and he will be happy. There will be no homesickness, no worrying about families, for all time and talents and interests are centered on the work of the ministry. Work, work, work. There is no satisfactory substitute, especially in missionary work."
And he said, "I try my best to just work."

He then said, "O" is for obedience. We must remember that obedience is the first law of heaven. Obedience is central to the gospel, and if a missionary is disobedient, he or she probably doesn't understand the gospel very well.

Obedience is a qualifier for the Holy Ghost, and obviously, if we don't have the Holy Ghost, we'll be teaching from our own knowledge and not from God. Therefore, we won't be able to teach with power and authority.

"I put obedience at the top of my priority list because I want to get the most out of my mission as I can. I want to help as many people as possible, and the only way to do that is through obedience."

Then the elder told me, "P" is for prayerful. As we're prayerful about our work, we are really counseling with the Lord. As we do this, we're able to be guided by the Spirit directly in every important thing.

Our planning, studies, finding, and teaching all become more directed and effective because we're being prayerful. Being prayerful is so important because as we communicate with Father in Heaven, He sees our faith and will help us and guide us and give us what we need in the very moment that we need it.
"I know HOP works." End quote.

So there you have it. That grandfather's advice about HOP is true. And I hope it's as helpful to you as it was for that great missionary who's gone on in his life and is doing great after his mission because HOP will work there too.
Elders and sisters, thanks for being so faithful. The Lord is pleased with your desires to do good and to be good.
Good night, stay focused, and stay positive.
